title: Emergency declaration should precede action but may follow it, or be withheld entirely for security
content:
A.1.9.1.5.5 empowers the Core Facilitator to declare an emergency "at their discretion, either on their own initiative or in response to a request from a community member," and then ranks three disclosure timings rather than mandating one.

The preferred case: "If the situation allows, the Core Facilitator should post the emergency declaration on the Sky Forum before taking action," with "sufficient detail regarding the issue and explaining why immediate action is required." The fallback: "If the urgency of the situation requires immediate intervention without delay, the Core Facilitator should create the Forum post as soon as possible after, or simultaneously with, the emergency action." The last resort: "There may be situations in which a public Emergency Declaration would be counterproductive to security objectives; the Core Facilitator is granted discretion in these matters."

This is the same graded-fallback structure the Atlas uses for adjudication reports (A.1.5.9.3.0.4.1) and for security-sensitive decision rationales (A.1.7.7). The pattern is consistent: state the transparency ideal, name the conditions under which it yields, and rank the degraded options so that the weakest is explicitly the last one.

The reason announce-before-acting is preferred is that it is the only ordering under which the community can object *while objection still matters*. A declaration published afterward is a notification, not a check. Preserving it as the default means the facilitator must judge each time whether urgency genuinely forecloses it, rather than treating post-hoc disclosure as normal.

The security exception is genuinely necessary — announcing that you are responding to an exploitable vulnerability can complete the attack — but it is also the least constrained clause in the Section, with no requirement to log the reason or disclose later once the risk passes. Compare A.1.6.6.0.3.1, which at least requires a facilitator to "document the basis" for delay.
